subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: Should macOS app-backed nodes be probed immediately on connect, deferred with readiness/backoff, or skipped when co-located with the gateway?
rationale: Current main now implements the macOS command handlers, so the remaining fix crosses readiness timing, co-location behavior, and retry/backoff product policy rather than a purely mechanical missing-handler repair.

options.title: Defer And Back Off Probes
options.body: Keep remote macOS skills supported, but delay initial app-node probes until readiness is stronger and add bounded retry/backoff for failed probes.

options.title: Skip Co-located App Nodes
options.body: Avoid probing loopback or same-host app nodes while preserving remote app-node probing for machines that can execute skills.

options.title: Disable App-node Probing By Default
options.body: Stop automatic app-node remote skill eligibility unless explicitly enabled, reducing warning churn at the cost of default remote skill support.

recommendation.title: Defer And Back Off Probes
recommendation.body: Keep remote macOS skills supported, but delay initial app-node probes until readiness is stronger and add bounded retry/backoff for failed probes.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history commits for mac node exec, remote skills hot reload, and the `system.which` probe make this the strongest routing owner for the policy choice.
